runs.title: ICE agent indicted: the charges and officials' word
runs.prompt: A Harris County grand jury in Houston, Texas has indicted ICE agent Mario Alberto Morales after an incident in which a man was allegedly hit by an ICE vehicle. Find out the exact charges Morales faces and what Harris County officials say happened. Report the facts and name the official source you relied on.
runs.answer: A Harris County grand jury indicted ICE agent Mario Alberto Morales on one count of second-degree felony aggravated assault with a deadly weapon — the deadly weapon being his vehicle; DA Sean Teare said a conviction carries 2 to 20 years in prison. The official source is the Harris County District Attorney's Office: DA Sean Teare announced the indictment at a press conference at the Harris County criminal courthouse with Harris County Sheriff Ed Gonzalez (his civil rights division chief Je'Rell Rogers presented the case to the grand jury). Teare said the evidence is "as clear as any that I've prosecuted or investigated" and that "this was an intentional strike, this was not an accident in any way, shape, or form." Per officials, on Oct. 10 in a parking lot near Clay Road and Highway 6, Miguel Parra-Hernandez, 48, ran from a truck during an ICE enforcement operation and Morales pursued him in a black SUV, swerving toward him and running over him; released body-camera video shows Morales saying "I was coming and I hit him with the car," and on his 911 call he said "I tried to get around him, and he hit my car" and that the man was "fine, he's just complaining of pain." runs.title: Zverev world No.1: confirm the win and the date
runs.prompt: Alexander Zverev is set to become men's tennis world No.1 after a win at the Vienna Open on 30 October 2026. Confirm the details: what result clinched the No.1 ranking for him, when exactly does the ranking become official, and who does he replace at the top of the ATP rankings?
runs.answer: Alexander Zverev clinched world No. 1 by beating Tallon Griekspoor 6-4, 7-5 in the round of 16 at the Erste Bank Open in Vienna (1h35m, 11 aces), a win that put him into the quarter-finals and made his ascent mathematically certain. One correction to the premise: that match was played on Thursday 29 October 2026, not 30 October — the 30 October date comes from Reuters/the BBC's write-up timing in some feeds, but the tournament's own report and the BBC both date the victory to 29 October. The ranking becomes official when the next PIF ATP Rankings are released on Monday, 2 November 2026, and he replaces Jannik Sinner at the top. Zverev becomes the 30th man to hold the ATP No. 1 ranking and the first German since Boris Becker in 1991, having already been assured of the year-end No. 1 spot but unable to overtake Sinner before that 2 November list.
